articles.title: Meet 17-year old Amara Wilson-Zegil who has taken robotics outreach to rural Ontario schools serving 1,800 children, helping run free or pay-what-you-can camps for 1,200 youth; she is now building a wider STEM access project
articles.summary: A teenager from Manitoulin Island, Ontario, is working to make science and technology more accessible to children who might otherwise miss out because of
articles.body: A teenager from Manitoulin Island, Ontario, is working to make science and technology more accessible to children who might otherwise miss out because of where they live or what their families can afford. Amara Wilson-Zegil, a Grade 11 student at Manitoulin Secondary School, has been named one of Canada’s Top 10 Youngest Changemakers of 2026 by Children First Canada for her efforts to expand access to science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM) education. According to Children First Canada’s announcement, also reported by ElliotLakeToday, the 17-year-old’s robotics outreach has reached six elementary schools serving more than 1,800 children. She has also helped deliver free and pay-what-you-can robotics camps that have reached more than 1,200 young people. Her work has now led her towards a broader initiative, Project RISE, short for the Rural Initiative for STEM Equity, which aims to address barriers to STEM learning in rural communities.Turning limited opportunities into a larger missionGrowing up in a rural area has given Wilson-Zegil a close view of how a child’s location can influence access to educational opportunities. While robotics and technology programmes can introduce students to practical problem-solving and emerging careers, such activities may be harder to access in communities with fewer local resources.Wilson-Zegil’s outreach has focused on bringing those experiences directly to elementary school students. Through robotics activities and camps, children can explore technology in a hands-on setting rather than encountering it only through classroom theory. The model also recognises that cost can prevent families from enrolling their children in extracurricular programmes. Offering free and pay-what-you-can camps helps make participation possible for young people whose families might not be able to afford conventional fees. The reach of the initiative, spanning six elementary schools and more than 1,200 camp participants, highlights the scale the student has already achieved while continuing her own education.Project RISE aims to widen access to STEMWilson-Zegil is now developing Project RISE to build on that experience and address the wider challenge of educational inequality in rural communities. The initiative’s focus is on making STEM opportunities less dependent on a student’s geographical location or household income. Its development marks a shift from individual outreach activities towards a broader effort to improve access to science and technology learning.The long-term significance of such programmes extends beyond robotics itself. Early exposure to STEM can help children develop analytical thinking, creativity and confidence in tackling unfamiliar problems. It can also introduce them to fields they may not otherwise consider pursuing. For rural students, these experiences can be particularly valuable when access to specialised clubs, equipment and extracurricular learning is limited.Recognition beyond the classroomAdditional reporting by Around and About highlights another dimension of Wilson-Zegil's work: she has captained an award-winning robotics programme involving approximately 100 students and authored a children's book about robotics, with proceeds supporting STEM programmes in rural communities.Wilson-Zegil received the Together We Rise Award for Equitable Education and Opportunities at Children First Canada's Future is NOW! Awards in Toronto on October 16. Each of the 10 young changemakers was set to receive $1,000 in funding, alongside mentorship, coaching and a year of support to help expand their initiatives. For Wilson-Zegil, the recognition brings national attention to a challenge that often receives less visibility: ensuring children in rural and Northern communities have opportunities to explore technology, develop new skills and imagine careers in fields that may seem distant from their everyday lives.Her next challenge is to turn that local impact into something larger through Project RISE, extending the possibility of hands-on STEM education to more young people across Northern Ontario.You use AI every day. articles.title: 12-year-old North Carolina boy with Kawasaki disease faces new battle after insurance denies scheduled heart procedure in Boston
articles.summary: A North Carolina family is preparing to take their 12-year-old son to Boston for a heart procedure despite an insurance denial that arrived just days
articles.body: A North Carolina family is preparing to take their 12-year-old son to Boston for a heart procedure despite an insurance denial that arrived just days before their scheduled trip to the hospital on October 19, ABC 13 reported. The insurer reportedly called the procedure “medically unnecessary and experimental”. The boy, who has already undergone open-heart surgery, requires the stent before his arteries narrow further, the family said. They did not have time to appeal before the trip and plan to fly out anyway.A tiredness that never went awayRowan Lowry was 7 when doctors diagnosed him with Kawasaki disease (KD). It is a disease that can cause damage to the heart and blood vessels, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). Mostly seen in children younger than 5, KD affects boys more often than girls. Its cause is unknown. In the US, the disease affects about 9 to 20 per 100,000 children under the age of 5, according to the agency.The first sign of KD is a fever that typically lasts for 5 days or longer. For Rowan, the initial sign was unusual tiredness, followed by a fever, his father, Joshua Lowry, previously told the outlet. Other symptoms include a rash; swelling and redness of the hands and feet; irritation and redness of the whites of the eyes; swollen lymph glands in the neck; and irritation and inflammation of the mouth, lips and throat.The family says the diagnosis came late. By the time doctors treated the disease, Rowan had developed multiple aortic aneurysms, which are weak, bulging spots in the body’s main artery. The 12-year-old has already undergone open-heart surgery. “This has become a lifelong battle for him, and for our family it is heartbreaking and frightening. We are all scared,” his father previously wrote on a GoFundMe page set up to raise funds for his treatment.Insurance denials can delay treatmentRowan is scheduled to undergo a stent procedure on Monday, October 19, at Boston Children’s Hospital. Days before the trip, the family’s insurer sent a denial letter. According to his mother, Cheryl Presnall, the insurer said the procedure was “deemed medically unnecessary and experimental”.“I got the letter of denial yesterday from our insurance, and they said that the cause of denial was because it is deemed medically unnecessary and experimental,” Presnall told the outlet. “Rowan is not a science experiment.”“They plan to put a stent in his left anterior descending artery in the hope of increasing his blood flow so he isn’t so tired all the time,” Rowan’s father explained on the fundraiser page.Without this procedure, Rowan’s condition would worsen. If the artery becomes too narrow for a stent, doctors may have to perform another open-heart surgery, his mother added. The family did not have time to appeal before the procedure date. They are going anyway.“We’re getting on the plane. Because at the end of the day, we’re going to do whatever we have to do. We’re going to fight,” his mother said.Miranda Yaver, an assistant professor at the University of Pittsburgh who studies insurance denials, says patients whose illnesses do not fit the textbook presentation of a condition often struggle to get care approved. “Things that maybe are lifesaving are ultimately getting denied because it’s not a textbook presentation of the condition,” Yaver said.The professor also points to the psychological toll that denial and appeal processes take on families.You use AI every day. articles.title: Trump endorses Netanyahu in Israeli legislative elections
articles.summary: In a social media post ahead of the October 27 election, Trump calls Netanyahu a ‘Strong, Brave, and Brilliant’ leader.
articles.body:
United States President Donald Trump has issued an endorsement of Israel’s incumbent Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who is facing a close race in parliamentary elections scheduled for October 27.

In a post on Truth Social on Sunday, Trump praised the Israeli leader for being an ally of the US in its war on Iran. He added that he was giving his “Complete and Total Endorsement” to Netanyahu.

“BIBI NETANYAHU WILL NEVER LET YOU DOWN!” Trump wrote.

The US president’s backing comes nine days before the Israeli election — and after speculation that it might not come at all.

Trump had refused to endorse Netanyahu earlier this month, when asked repeatedly about the Israeli leader’s job performance in an interview with Time magazine.

Instead, when pressed by his interviewer, Trump avoided the subject, shifting the focus instead to his own popularity or security in the Middle East.

The two leaders have met more than a half dozen times since January 2025, but there have been reports of disagreements, including over the war against Iran and other conflicts.

In June, Trump acknowledged calling Netanyahu “f***ing crazy” in a phone conversation where he expressed frustration about Israel’s attacks on Lebanon.

Trump had reportedly asked Netanyahu not to take further action in Lebanon, in an apparent attempt to preserve a short-lived April ceasefire with Iran.

The two leaders had jointly launched a war against Iran on February 28, but the conflict has cost Trump domestic support.

The war has upended the global oil and gas supply, with no clear end in sight.

A Pew Research Center poll found this month that roughly two-thirds of US voters disapprove of Trump’s handling of the war, which has driven up consumer fuel prices and raised concerns about draining military stockpiles.

Trump’s Republican Party is facing a critical midterm election on November 3 that will decide whether it maintains control of the US Congress, as well as other key state and local offices.

Experts have speculated that Trump’s prior reticence to endorse Netanyahu may have come from public perception that Israel may have coaxed the US into the war.

Netanyahu’s Likud Party and its far-right coalition are also facing the prospect of losing the October contest to an opposition bloc led by Yashar party head Gadi Eisenkot.

But despite reports of fraying relations, Trump told the news outlet Axios on Sunday that his endorsement of Netanyahu was never in doubt.

“I was always going to do that. I just didn’t want to do it too soon,” Trump said in a short telephone interview to the publication, adding: “It is important that Israel has a person they can count on.”

Axios said it questioned Trump about whether he could work with another Israeli leader other than Netanyahu. The US president answered evasively.

“Maybe I will, maybe I won’t. Who wants to take the chance?” Trump replied.

In his social media post announcing the endorsement, Trump also defended his and Netanyahu’s decision to initiate the war against Iran. The president argued it was only a matter of time before Iran would have attacked both the US and Israel.

The war, Trump argued, had already left Iran “systematically destroyed, both Militarily and Financially, and unless they change their ways, rapidly, we will soon finish the job”.

“If Israel has the wrong Leader, which would be anyone other than Bibi, America will have to do this work ourselves, and I am not inclined to do so,” Trump wrote.

“Bibi Netanyahu has been Strong, Brave, and Brilliant in the face of tremendous opposition, including that coming from even Israel, itself.”

In response to the post, Netanyahu posted a video on social media expressing gratitude to the US president.

“I’m so honoured and humbled by your extraordinary endorsement,” Netanyahu said. “There’s never been a greater friend of Israel in the White House. That’s an understatement.”

Netanyahu also praised Trump for not being “set back by internal criticism” about the war against Iran. He directed several of his comments to US voters, in an attempt to offer support for Trump’s Republican Party amid questions about the rising cost of living.

“Let me say to the American people: If you are worried about today’s gas prices, think of what will happen if Iran gets nuclear weapons, something that Donald Trump and I will never allow,” Netanyahu said.

“When that threat of that regime disappears, gas prices will go down, and how. But only under Trump. It’s not going to happen with those who want to accommodate and appease these tyrants.”

articles.title: Centre issues advisory to Meta, asks it to overhaul content promotion system on Facebook, Instagram
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Centre has directed social media giant Meta, which owns Instagram and Facebook, to ensure that its recommendation algorithms do not result
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Centre has directed social media giant Meta, which owns Instagram and Facebook, to ensure that its recommendation algorithms do not result in "disproportionate exposure of users to a single or limited set of narratives.""Ensure that recommendation systems do not result in disproportionate exposure of users to a single or limited set of narratives, and endeavour to provide appropriate diversity of relevant and credible information," an advisory issued by the ministry of electronics and information technology (MeitY), dated October 10, stated, PTI reported."Also strengthen mechanisms for rapid identification, review and escalation of content, which is gaining significant reach through recommendation systems and has the potential to cause widespread public confusion, apprehension, violence or disturbance of public order," it added.While the advisory does not cite any specific incident that led to its issuance, it comes amid ongoing protests in Delhi demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.MeitY also asked Meta to cooperate with law enforcement and other authorised government agencies by providing information or assistance within the timelines prescribed under the IT Rules, 2021.The ministry noted that certain content relating to "ongoing public events" was being "prominently displayed and recommended to users" on Meta platforms.Citing the Information Technology Act, 2000, the advisory highlighted the company’s obligation to exercise due diligence under the IT Rules, 2021, which require intermediaries to inform users about prohibited content, including material likely to cause public disorder or incite a cognisable offence.MeitY also flagged content presenting old or selectively edited visuals as current events, misleading claims about emergencies, restrictions or police action, and audio-visual material depicting law-and-order situations without adequate context. It also raised concerns over content likely to incite violence and misleading material receiving disproportionate amplification.The advisory outlined six requirements for Meta, including measures to identify and address prohibited content and review recommendation and ranking systems to ensure misleading, manipulated or out-of-context material is not "disproportionately amplified or repeatedly recommended to users".MeitY emphasised that the advisory seeks to promote responsible information dissemination while respecting lawful expression and public discourse."Meta is advised to ensure that any action taken pursuant to this advisory is consistent with the Information Technology Act, 2000, the IT Rules, 2021, and other applicable laws," the ministry added.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Bimol Akoijam willing to contest Manipur Assembly polls if Congress offers ticket
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Congress MP Angomcha Bimol Akoijam on Sunday said he was willing to contest next year's Manipur Assembly elections from the Keishamthong
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Congress MP Angomcha Bimol Akoijam on Sunday said he was willing to contest next year's Manipur Assembly elections from the Keishamthong constituency if the party offered him a ticket, as he faces a sexual harassment case and has been dismissed from Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU).Speaking at an event, the Inner Manipur MP said his decision to enter the electoral contest would be guided by the future of the state."I am ready to fight elections from Keishamthong (in Imphal West district). If the party offers me a ticket, I will contest the Keisamthong assembly constituency. This decision is for the future of the state," Akoijam said, according to news agency PTI.The Manipur Assembly elections are due next year.His remarks come amid an ongoing police investigation into sexual harassment allegations against him and his dismissal from JNU, where he was a professor at the Centre for the Study of Social Systems under the School of Social Sciences.JNU dismissal and police investigationAkoijam was dismissed from the university on October 9 following an inquiry into allegations of sexual harassment. He has denied the charges and described the university's action as a "witch hunt", claiming he was not given an opportunity to respond to the inquiry committee's findings.Delhi Police booked him on October 11 following a complaint by JNU's chief security officer. He recently appeared before investigators at the Vasant Kunj North Police Station in New Delhi in connection with the case.At least 11 female students submitted complaints against Akoijam in May. They alleged that he invited students to his campus residence on the pretext of meetings or gatherings and attempted to harass them. Some students also alleged that he made obscene and inappropriate remarks in class.After appearing before investigators, Akoijam said he intended to challenge his dismissal legally.Speaking to reporters in Imphal on Friday, he said his lawyers were preparing the case and that he would file it within a day or two.He also said he had cooperated with the police and would continue to do so, while requesting adequate notice for any further questioning because of his responsibilities as an MP.Akoijam says Manipur's wider crisis needs attentionDuring his remarks to the media, Akoijam also urged greater attention to the wider situation in Manipur, including the plight of internally displaced people, lawlessness and issues surrounding buffer zones."Thousands of people are languishing in relief camps. I don’t think my pain is anything greater than the pain of these people," he said, while alleging that the action against him was an attempt to silence his voice.The MP had earlier said, "Justice will be done," before travelling to New Delhi to join the police investigation.The allegations have also triggered political reactions in the state. BJP workers staged a protest outside Congress Bhavan in Imphal, demanding Akoijam's resignation and accusing him of bringing disrepute to Manipur. Police prevented the protesters from entering the premises.Congress spokesperson Hareshwar Goshwami described the protest as a diversionary tactic and accused the ruling party of deflecting attention from killings and the crisis in the state.Akoijam has maintained that the allegations against him are false and has challenged the process that led to his dismissal. The sexual harassment allegations remain under investigation.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: In 2017, a Michigan father turned free Halloween decorations into a backyard attraction that he says drew 18,000 visitors in 2024; nine years later, a neighbour's complaint sparked a dispute with the city
articles.summary: In 2017, Nate Taylor found a three-word offer on Craigslist for free Halloween decorations. It took three truck trips to bring everything home.
articles.body: In 2017, Nate Taylor found a three-word offer on Craigslist for free Halloween decorations. It took three truck trips to bring everything home. Nearly a decade later, that secondhand collection has become a local attraction that drew an estimated 18,000 visitors last October and led to a legal dispute with city officials in Michigan. Taylor, a 49-year-old part-time DJ and stay-at-home father, spends weeks setting up detailed Halloween displays outside his Cape Cod-style home near Kid's Creek Park in Traverse City. Known as Dead Ends on Spruce, the annual attraction features 25 moving Halloween figures, called animatronics, ranging from 6 to 12 feet tall. They include a 7-foot werewolf and a 12-foot headless horseman. The display also uses 40 speakers to play sounds of rain and thunder, along with a custom fog system that runs through 400 feet of trenches in the yard.Origins and focus on accessibilityThe display began when Taylor answered a classified ad from a local resident who was downsizing after a divorce and giving away 20 years' worth of holiday decorations. “Really, ma'am? You want us to take this?” Taylor recalled asking in an interview published by Realtor.com. After bringing the decorations home, Taylor tied a tarp to a large tree branch in his 40-foot-wide yard to protect items that were not made to withstand the weather. Over the years, he added more covered areas, built a graveyard with headstones, and began running the lights and sound systems throughout the evening. Taylor created the attraction to give families and children with special needs a safe place to enjoy Halloween for free. As the father of two children on the autism spectrum, he said that options for neurodivergent children and young people during the autumn holiday season are often limited in the region. “I'm not into blood and gore or jump scares,” Taylor told Realtor.com. He added that his goal was to create an event that is “easily accessible and free” to the local special needs community. “We have never charged a dime, not one, for any ticket,” he added.Municipal letters and legal disputesBy 2024, support from neighbors had helped create a social media page for the property. The attraction drew an estimated 18,000 visitors and six school groups during October. Taylor took a break in 2025 to care for family members, including his mother while she received treatment for colon cancer. When he prepared to reopen in August 2026, Taylor met with local fire marshals and the city manager responsible for enforcing local rules. He asked the city to close the street each Halloween night to improve safety. After one neighbor complained that Taylor was running a commercial business by selling admission tickets, the city sent him a four-page legal letter explaining local rules for businesses run from homes. One restriction limited the property to no more than eight car trip ends at any given time. “They think I am a business,” Taylor told Realtor.com. “I am not.” Realtor.com reported that city officials did not immediately respond to requests for comment about the enforcement action. Taylor argued that the city had acted on an unverified tip. He said that when visitor numbers were spread across 30 days, the traffic was similar to that of a large garage sale and did not block neighbors' driveways. To pay for the display after taking a year off, Taylor accepted about $400 in online contributions through Venmo and sold some of his personal DJ equipment. He maintained that visitors could still enter the yard entirely for free.Continued operations and community responseAfter three attorneys offered to represent him for free, Taylor's legal team sent a formal letter asking city officials to explain their plans for enforcing the rules by September 18. “We never heard back,” Taylor said. After receiving no further response from local officials, Dead Ends on Spruce opened as planned for the October season. Taylor said about 400 people attended opening night, and 25 special needs groups had booked visits throughout the month. “We haven't had one city official come,” Taylor told Realtor.com. “It has been absolutely successful.” Taylor expects the total number of visitors to reach nearly 25,000 by the end of the season.You use AI every day. articles.title: Service member dies after falling during pregame demonstration at college football game
articles.summary: A service member fell during a pregame aerial demonstration in San Antonio on Saturday night and later died at a hospital, according to military officials and video verified by NBC News.
articles.body: A service member fell during a pregame aerial demonstration in San Antonio on Saturday night and later died at a hospital, according to military officials and video verified by NBC News. Video recorded from the stands shows the service member descending on a rope from the stadium’s rafters before falling to the field. Spectators are seen watching the field at the stadium in downtown San Antonio, where the University of Texas at San Antonio defeated the Naval Academy after a delayed kickoff. The service member, who was not identified, was transported to a local hospital and later died, a Nellis Air Force Base spokesperson said in a statement. The incident is under investigation. The service member was assigned to the U.S. Air Force’s 6th Combat Training Squadron, Detachment 2, according to the statement. An individual raced from the sidelines toward the service member as he laid lifeless at the 50-yard line. The service member was driven off the field in a golf cart as fans watched in horror. The University of Texas at San Antonio had scheduled events at the game to honor service members and veterans. “We are deeply saddened by the incident that occurred at the start of tonight’s football game,” UT-San Antonio said in a statement Saturday night. “Our heartfelt thoughts and prayers are with the soldier who was affected, his family and his military colleagues.” The city of San Antonio, which owns the Alamodome, did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Sunday.

articles.body: NEW DELHI: Saurabh Bharadwaj has accused Delhi Police of harassing the Bengali community and Durga Puja committees in Chittaranjan Park (CR Park), alleging that police personnel forcibly disconnected electricity at a pandal and damaged equipment. articles.title: Hurricane Trudy brings heavy rain and strong winds to Mexico’s Pacific coast
articles.summary: Hurricane Trudy lashed parts of Mexico’s Pacific coast with heavy rain and strong winds Sunday but was forecast to move away, the U.S.
articles.body: MIAMI — Hurricane Trudy lashed parts of Mexico’s Pacific coast with heavy rain and strong winds Sunday but was forecast to move away, the U.S. National Hurricane Center said. The Category 2 hurricane was packing maximum sustained winds of 105 mph (165 kph) and moving northwest at 8 mph (13 kph). Trudy’s center was expected to remain near the Mexican coast through Sunday evening before moving south of the Baja California Peninsula on Monday and Tuesday. A tropical storm warning remained in effect for Las Islas Marias and for the region between Playa Perula and San Blas. The Mexican navy urged mariners and coastal residents to exercise extreme caution because of high waves, heavy rain and the risk of rising rivers, flooding and landslides in vulnerable areas. Colima authorities said the risks remained low, but warned that heavy rainfall could cause damage because the ground was already saturated by successive storms along the Pacific coast. Trudy was expected to bring 4-8 inches (10-20 centimeters) of rain through the weekend, with isolated totals of around 12 inches (30 centimeters) along and near the coast in Michoacan, Colima and Jalisco. The hurricane center warned of potentially life-threatening flooding and mudslides, especially in areas with steep terrain. Typhoon Champi blows away from Guam Also in the Pacific, Typhoon Champi was moving away from Guam on Sunday after passing close to the island’s southern tip, with sustained winds of 150 mph (240 kph). Late Sunday afternoon it was 190 miles (305 kilometers) west of Guam, moving west at 14 mph (23 kph), according to the U.S. National Weather Service. Champi is forecast to decrease in intensity on Sunday then potentially increase to Category 5 typhoon by Monday evening, the Federal Emergency Management Agency, a department of the U.S. Department of Homeland Security, said. All tropical cyclone watches and warnings for Guam, Rota, Tinian and Saipan had been canceled. The governors of Guam and the Northern Mariana Islands requested emergency disaster declarations on Friday. On Saturday, U.S. President Donald Trump approved an emergency declaration for Guam authorizing FEMA to coordinate all federal disaster relief efforts. FEMA announced that federal disaster assistance was available for the territory of Guam to supplement local response efforts following Typhoon Champi. Airports, harbors and some health facilities in the territories were closed. Relief supplies were unlikely to reach the islands for three to five days, according to Saturday updates from FEMA. The territories are still recovering from super typhoons Sinlaku and Bavi, which struck in April and July, respectively.

articles.title: Canadian PM Carney says 4 service members killed, dozens injured in military base fire
articles.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney confirmed four service members died after fierce 62 mph winds fueled flames at CFB Wainwright, Alberta.
articles.body: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney announced Sunday that four service members were killed and dozens more seriously injured after a fire broke out during military training at a base in Alberta, calling it one of the country's worst peacetime military tragedies on domestic soil. The deadly fire erupted Saturday at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright, where fierce winds fueled flames that spread beyond the installation and into surrounding rural areas. Canadian military officials said there were no indications of terrorism, though the cause remained under investigation. Carney said in a televised address that the families of the four service members killed had been notified and that the situation was still evolving. AT LEAST 1 KILLED, 34 FIREFIGHTERS AND EMS WORKERS INJURED IN 'MAJOR' STATEN ISLAND SHIPYARD EXPLOSION: FDNY The prime minister said those affected included reservists and soldiers from Princess Patricia's Canadian Light Infantry, one of Canada's oldest military regiments. Personnel had traveled from bases across the country to participate in training exercises at Wainwright. Canadian Defense Minister David McGuinty initially confirmed fatalities and injuries but did not provide a casualty count, Fox News Digital previously reported. "I cannot recall such an incident in my short time for sure as a minister, but I cannot recall an incident like this in recent memory," McGuinty told reporters. The exact number of injured service members remained unclear Sunday, with victims receiving treatment at hospitals in Wainwright, Edmonton, Red Deer and Calgary. Several hospitals across Alberta activated a "Code Orange," an emergency designation for mass-casualty incidents, as medical personnel scrambled to treat the wounded. "This number of patients would overwhelm the city of Edmonton," Dr. Warren Thirsk, an emergency department physician at Royal Alexandra Hospital, told CBC News. "It is more patients than any of us want to count right now. It's a disaster." MARINE CORPS OSPREY CATCHES FIRE DURING EXERCISE IN NORTH CAROLINA; 4 INJURED The Royal Canadian Mounted Police said officers responded to reports of a fire in a training area at the base shortly after 4 p.m. Saturday. Firefighters battled intense winds, with gusts reaching up to 62 mph, as flames spread beyond the installation. By late Saturday, local officials said the fire was being held and that property and critical infrastructure were protected. No evacuation order had been issued for nearby residents. McGuinty said the RCMP was involved in investigating the incident, describing the situation as "very, very active and delicate." He also praised emergency crews who battled the flames through the night. Fox News Digital's Michael Sinkewicz and The Associated Press contributed to this report.

articles.summary: Tim Walz says he decided not to seek re-election over Minnesota's fraud scandal, calling it a "gift" to Republicans seeking to cut social programs.
articles.body: Gov. Tim Walz took responsibility for mishandling fraud in Minnesota even as he took multiple parting shots at the Trump administration. During Friday’s episode of "The Lever" podcast, Walz said that he lacked the authority to independently stop payments to suspected fraudsters and needed legislative action to obtain that authority, but nonetheless acknowledged that his administration should have acted sooner. "The amount of fraud, like I said, $1 is too much, but the amount that has been prosecuted, and people put in jail, is less than what [President Donald Trump] is asking for his ballroom," Walz said. When pressed further by the host about whether he was worried that the fraud allegations would continue to be damaging, Walz replied, "Yes. They undermine faith in government." He added, "It's one of the reasons I accept responsibility for that. I think, you know, I had decided, probably after the murder of Melissa Hortman, certainly before Christmas, that we weren't going to run again because I said, ‘They're going to use this to attack others and to attack the system.’" GOP ACCUSES WALZ ALLIES OF BURYING $52M MEDICAID FRAUD REPORT BEFORE ELECTION "Every state has this. Most states have far more than this," he added. "The Trump administration decided to focus on the perfect storm for them," Walz said. "‘Blame Somalis.’ ‘Blame the guy who ran against me.’ ‘Blame this prosperous state that pays more money in than not and let's punish them.’ But that doesn't excuse that. Should we do more? Yes. Were there things that we should have closed back doors sooner? Yes. I mean, it happened. Now we know other states are learning from us." He later said, "The problem with fraud and corruption, both of them undermine faith in government, and that plays right into Republicans' hands. Do they like fraud? I would argue they do because it undermines federal. It makes a reason to cut these programs. They hate these programs that feed children. They hate these programs that, you know, work with autistic children. So, man, what a gift to them. ‘See, they don't work. It's tax dollars. Let's close them down.’" TRUMP IS FIGHTING OBAMACARE FRAUD. "These excuses insult our intelligence," he said of Walz's statements. "The governor has ample authority to stop payments when there's evidence of fraud. The governor can also refer the evidence to state and federal prosecutors for immediate action. The reality here is that this systemic fraud seemed to be going on for over a decade with officials like Tim Walz and Peggy Flanagan doing almost nothing about it. And there are serious questions as to whether they turned a blind eye because the beneficiaries of the fraud were voting for them, contributing to their campaigns, we're helping them politically in some way. The real question is whether these senior officials were somehow benefiting directly or indirectly." "They were in charge while foreigners and criminals pilfered billions in public funds, and Democrats let it all happen. Now they deflect and blame Republicans. You can’t make it make sense," Wold said. "Republicans want government to work for American citizens. articles.title: Neemuch police bust cyber fraud gang, arrest four
articles.summary: Neemuch police bust interstate cyber fraud gang promising stock tips; 4 arrested, 62 ATM cards, cheque books, mobiles, laptop seized; Rs 51,500 recovered.
articles.body: Indore: Neemuch police have busted an interstate cyber fraud racket that allegedly cheated people by promising stock market trading tips and high returns, arresting four and recovering 62 ATM cards, nine cheque books, eight passbooks, eight mobile phones, an ATM swipe machine, a sedan, a laptop, a MacBook and Rs 51,500 in cash.The action was carried out jointly by Neemuch Cyber Cell and Neemuch City police. The actions were taken after the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C), under the Union home ministry, shared data through the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal (NCRP) regarding suspicious mule bank accounts, ATM withdrawal accounts and their associates.Police said the operation was carried out on the basis of technical data and informer inputs identifying different ATM withdrawal locations linked to suspicious bank accounts. On Oct 16 and 17, police detained Nikhil Kumawat, Deepak Meghwal and Jayant Kumawat near banks and ATM booths for questioning.During interrogation, the three allegedly revealed that they had given their bank account kits and account kits belonging to other people to Alkesh Panwar. Panwar allegedly used these mule accounts to receive money obtained through cyber frauds.According to police, the gang had created a website, and operated through a fake office, social media platforms and phone calls. The accused allegedly approached people with promises of stock market trading tips and high profits and persuaded them to transfer money into the mule accounts.Acting on the disclosures of the three accused, police detained Panwar and recovered 62 ATM cards, eight passbooks, eight cheque books, an ATM swipe machine, eight mobile phones, a car and Rs 51,500 in cash. The seizure also included one laptop and one MacBook.The three accused are residents of Kacholi village under Jeeran police station while Panwar is a resident of Star City Colony on Mhow Road in Neemuch.Police said the recovered ATM cards, passbooks and cheque books belonged to different banks and their connection with various accounts is being examined.A case has been registered at Neemuch City police station under relevant sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and Information Technology Act.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Indore | Silver Rate in Indore | Bank Holidays in Indore | Public Holidays in Indore | Petrol Price in Indore | Diesel Price in Indore | CNG Price in Indore | LPG Price in IndoreStay updated with the latest Indore news. articles.body: Chandigarh: Punjab BJP president Kewal Singh Dhillon on Sunday announced that he would wear a black turban until justice is delivered in the murder case of anti-drug activist Parvinder Singh Jhota.Wearing a black turban, Dhillon, in a video message, said that while participating in the ongoing protest over Jhota’s murder in Mansa on Saturday, he had appealed to the people of Punjab to register their protest by wearing black turbans and black dupattas and carrying black flags until justice was delivered.Jhota’s father Bhim Singh and the people participating in the protest accepted the appeal, Dhillon said.He said, “What has happened to a young man who raised his voice against drugs has deeply shaken the people of Punjab. A young man who was fighting to save Punjab’s youth from drugs was brutally murdered. This is not merely the murder of Parvinder Singh; it is also the murder of law and order in Punjab.”Dhillon said he had joined the protest as “a member of the bereaved family’s extended family”.The Punjab BJP chief said the black turban was “not merely a piece of clothing but a symbol of protest against the govt’s failure”. He said peaceful protests and the struggle for justice would continue until the family received full justice.“The BJP stands firmly with the family and will raise its voice for justice at every level,” he said.Dhillon alleged, “Instead of curbing drugs, the AAP govt was trying to silence those who raise their voices against the menace.”He further alleged, “Gulzar Singh of Toor Banjara, who had spoken out against drugs, was earlier driven to suicide, followed by the murder of Parvinder Singh Jhota. articles.title: Enrolment in Rohtas govt schools stagnant for 3 years
articles.summary: Rohtas district govt school enrolment stayed near 4.45 lakh for 3 years, with rises in Classes I and IX, declines in II-V and X-XI, officials say.
articles.body: Sasaram: Student enrolment in govt schools across Rohtas district has remained stagnant at around 4.45 lakh over the past three academic years, even as individual classes recorded sharp increases and declines, according to education department figures.Total enrolment from Classes I to XII stood at 4,45,629 in 2024-25, fell to 4,44,846 in 2025-26 and rose marginally to 4,45,124 in 2026-27. The latest figure is 278 higher than the previous academic year but 505 below the 2024-25 level.District Information Officer (DIO) Madan Rai said the overall enrolment figure had not changed significantly over the past three years, though there were variations across classes. He said enrolment had declined in some classes and increased in others, and the department would review the variations to ascertain the reasons.However, class-wise figures show substantial variations. Class I enrolment has more than doubled from 15,306 in 2024-25 to 30,874 in 2026-27, an increase of 15,568 students. Class IX recorded an even sharper rise, with enrolment increasing by 19,907, from 16,840 to 36,747 over the same period.Class VI enrolment increased by 4,013, from 34,751 in 2024-25 to 38,764 in 2026-27. Class XII also recorded a substantial increase, from 21,693 students in 2024-25 to 38,875 in 2026-27. However, the latest figure was lower than the 40,129 students recorded in 2025-26.In contrast, enrolment declined in Classes II to V. Class II recorded a fall of 818 students, Class III 11,672, Class IV 12,434 and Class V 12,142 over the three-year period. Class II enrolment fell from 35,146 in 2024-25 to 30,823 in 2025-26 before recovering to 34,328 in 2026-27. Class III enrolment declined from 45,373 in 2024-25 to 33,701 in 2026-27.Classes X and XI also recorded declines of 7,968 and 8,203 students, respectively. Class VIII had 44,750 students in 2024-25. Enrolment declined the following year before recovering in 2026-27, though the report does not provide the figures for the latter two years in the copy.Block-wise figures also reveal contrasting trends. Dinara recorded an increase of 4,682 students, followed by Nokha with 1,759, Tilouthu with 1,647 and Karghar with 1,393. Bikramganj recorded a decline of 3,030 students, followed by Kochas with 2,141, Sasaram with 1,618 and Nasriganj with 1,585.Meanwhile, a senior education department official, requesting anonymity, said poor infrastructure and the quality of education in govt schools were forcing parents to send their children to nearby private schools.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Patna | Silver Rate in Patna | Bank Holidays in Patna | Public Holidays in Patna | Patna AQI | Weather in Patna | Petrol Price in Patna | Diesel Price in Patna | CNG Price in Patna | LPG Price in PatnaStay updated with the latest Patna news. articles.title: Kolkata Woman Defrauded of Rs 61 Lakh by Fake NIA Officers in Mumbai
articles.summary: Kolkata woman alleges fake NIA officers in Mumbai extorted Rs 61 lakh via 10-day “digital arrest” terror funding threat; police seek to freeze accounts.
articles.body: Mumbai: A 67-year-old Kolkata woman has alleged that fraudsters posing as National Investigation Agency (NIA) officers from the Mumbai office extorted Rs 61 lakh from her by threatening to arrest her over purported terror financing and keeping her under “digital arrest” for 10 days.She lodged a complaint with Khar police on Friday after reaching her daughter’s home in Bandra (West) on Oct 14 with the callers’ permission. Her daughter noticed she was distressed and learnt that she had lost her lifetime savings and mortgaged gold ornaments to pay the fraudsters.A Khar police officer said the woman received WhatsApp video calls between Oct 1 and 10 from fraudsters claiming to be from the office of an NIA deputy inspector general in Colaba. They alleged that a bank account opened in her name in Andheri was being used to finance a terrorist organisation and that an FIR and arrest warrant had been issued against her.Although she denied owning the account, she believed the caller after he recited her Aadhaar number. To frighten her, the fraudsters sent a video purportedly showing police officers assaulting four alleged members of the organisation and claimed they had identified her as a financier. “The callers instructed me not to tell anyone or leave home without permission. After obtaining my bank details, they demanded Rs 25 lakh, which I transferred through RTGS on Oct 3. I transferred another Rs 7 lakh on Oct 5 after they claimed the first payment was insufficient,” said the senior citizen in the FIR.When she said she had no money left, the fraudsters asked about her jewellery. Following their directions, she removed ornaments from her bank locker, obtained a loan of Rs 29.9 lakh and transferred Rs 29 lakh to a specified account on Oct 8.Police have asked the bank’s nodal officer to freeze the Delhi accounts that received the money. The Mumbai cyber police registered five FIRs between Sept 10 and Oct 1 after fraudsters allegedly placed five senior citizens under “digital arrest” and cheated them of Rs 2.28 crore by threatening to implicate them with a terrorist outfit, linking their names with terrorism and funding them. Scammers also force victims to write and send WhatsApp messages declaring that they are not a threat to national security. The victims, aged between 61 and 86 and from Chunabhatti, Kandivli, Malad, Mulund and Powai, who are retired teachers, bankers and govt employees, were allegedly kept under video-call surveillance, in some cases for more than a week. Fraudsters claimed their Aadhaar cards, bank accounts or identities had been misused to obtain SIM cards, open accounts or finance terrorism. The terrorist name used and linked with the victims is “Asif Fauji”.A cyber expert said cyberattacks in India had increased more than five times since 2019 and most victims never recovered their money. Companies, banks and govt offices needed trained personnel to protect systems and prevent attacks, the expert said. articles.title: London woman bought a £600,000 semi-detached home in 2021; a year later she challenged her neighbours’ kitchen for crossing the boundary by 48cm, but a tribunal has now ruled the tiny strip belongs to them
articles.summary: A London homeowner has lost a four-year legal battle over a strip of land measuring just 48 centimetres after a tribunal ruled that her neighbours’
articles.body: A London homeowner has lost a four-year legal battle over a strip of land measuring just 48 centimetres after a tribunal ruled that her neighbours’ kitchen extension had acquired “squatters’ rights.” Susannah James bought the £600,000 semi-detached house in Surbiton in 2021, but a year later claimed that part of the adjoining property’s kitchen had been built across the boundary onto her land. The First-tier Tribunal has now found in favour of neighbours Mina Sharma and Neil Deeley, who will not have to demolish the disputed section of their kitchen. The ruling was reported by The Independent and AOL. Read more details about it here:A tiny strip, a major disputeThe homes in Cottage Grove, Surbiton, were once part of a single Victorian property before being divided into two semi-detached houses. Both properties have single-storey kitchen extensions at the rear. While the boundary between the two kitchens follows the garden fence line, the roof line of the houses reveals that the neighbours’ kitchen “steps” across the boundary by 48 centimetres. According to the tribunal, nobody had noticed the discrepancy for around 40 years. Thick vegetation at the rear of the properties obscured the border, and even Mrs James said, as per reports, that she did not realise when she bought her home that she might be acquiring a small part of her neighbour’s kitchen.Mrs James, a Cambridge-educated tax company boss, and her husband and business partner Chris James asked Judge Ewan Paton to declare that the slice of the neighbours’ kitchen was trespassing on their land. They sought an order requiring it to be demolished and removed, as per reports.Why the neighbours wonThe kitchen extension is believed to have been built in the early 1980s, long before Ms Sharma and Mr Deeley purchased their home in 2012. Evidence from a previous joint owner indicated that the extension had been in the same position since at least 2000. The judge described the evidence as “overwhelming” that the kitchen had remained in that location for well over two decades before the dispute began, it was reported.Ms Sharma and Mr Deeley did not argue that the original boundary line was different. Instead, they claimed adverse possession, commonly known as squatters’ rights, over the 48-centimetre strip. The tribunal accepted that successive owners had physically possessed the land and reasonably believed it belonged to them because their kitchen was built on it.Judge Paton said, reported The Independent, that the construction and enjoyment of part of a house on neighbouring land was “possibly the plainest example” of factual possession combined with an intention to possess. He found that the neighbours had been in adverse possession of the strip since at least October 2000.What the judge saidThe judge acknowledged that property boundaries are not always perfectly straight in practice. He noted that Ordnance Survey and Land Registry index maps can contain kinks, curves and steps, and that ordinary buyers cannot reasonably be expected to spot every minor discrepancy simply because a physical boundary appears slightly uneven.In comments reported by The Independent, Judge Paton said a purchaser is entitled to assume that “what they see is what they get” when buying a home whose boundaries appear as seen on the ground. He added that it was entirely reasonable for successive owners to believe they owned everything within the walls of their property. He also said the case showed the importance of long-established physical boundaries in resolving disputes. Because the extension had likely stood in the same place for more than 22 years before the issue was raised, the tribunal approved the neighbours’ application for adverse possession of the land.A costly lesson for homeownersThe ruling means Mrs James and Chris James cannot force their neighbours to remove or demolish the section of kitchen that crosses the boundary. Although the disputed land is tiny, the case demonstrates how a small encroachment can become a serious legal issue when title plans, physical boundaries and long-standing structures do not align.For buyers, the case is a reminder that a property’s registered title plan may not perfectly match what exists on the ground. Fences, extensions, garden walls and older buildings can all create small differences that remain unnoticed for decades.Boundary experts often advise buyers to check title plans carefully, commission a survey before completing a purchase, and raise concerns early if an extension, wall or fence appears to sit unusually close to a neighbour’s property. Once a structure has remained in place openly and without challenge for many years, the legal position can become far more difficult to reverse.The Surbiton case may have involved less than half a metre of land, but it ended with a clear message from the tribunal: long-established physical boundaries can carry significant legal weight, even when they differ from the line shown on paper.You use AI every day. articles.title: UT spends less than half of capital budget in first 6 months
articles.summary: Chandigarh UT spent 55.5% of its 2026-27 budget in April-Sept; capital spending lagged at 45.1% vs 56.6% under revenue head.
articles.body: Chandigarh: The Chandigarh administration has failed to spend even 50% of the annual budget allocated under the capital head by the Centre in the first six months of the 2026-27 financial year. The administration has spent just around 45.1% in the capital segment, which is meant for infrastructure, buildings and related developmental works.However, the authority has spent around 56.6% of the budget in the revenue head, which is meant for committed liabilities like salaries, wages, allowances, travel, medical reimbursement, etc.According to UT records, Rs 273.79 crore of the Rs 606 crore allocated in the capital head has been spent so far this financial year. In the revenue category, Rs 3,364 crore of the Rs 5,939.5 crore allocated has been spent.Over the six-month period of the current fiscal, the administration has spent Rs 3,638.06 crore collectively under the capital and revenue heads from the total allocated amount of Rs 6,545 crore. This marks around 55.5% of the total allocation.However, lower expenditure under the capital segment has raised a serious question over the UT’s developmental plan in the current financial year. Data revealed that 79.1% expenditure was incurred on infrastructural assets but just 47.9% of the work was done under the building and structures segment.In other capital expenditure, only 9.3% expenditure was incurred. In the revenue segment, over 50% expenditure was registered in the salaries and allowances segments, while wages and medical allowance registered over 40% expenditure.“Largely, works under the capital segment, like infrastructural development, project construction, buildings etc are under the UT engineering department, which remains under constant monitoring. The UT finance department also reviews planned and proposed works from time to time,” sources said.Sources in the Chandigarh administration revealed that the expenditure report of six months, April to Sept, is shared with the MHA. articles.title: City cops nab Guj woman who stole gems worth ₹2cr
articles.summary: Jaipur police arrested a Gujarat woman for stealing ₹2 crore in emeralds from a trader on an e-rickshaw; gems recovered after CCTV-led probe.
articles.body: Jaipur: Police have arrested a woman from Gujarat and recovered Rs 2 crore worth of precious gemstones she allegedly lifted from a trader while he was travelling by e-rickshaw through the crowded markets of the Walled City.Police said the woman was so skilled at stealing items from unsuspecting people on the streets that the trader did not realise he had been robbed until several hours after the crime. Her identity is being withheld due to the ongoing nature of the investigation.DCP (North) Karan Sharma said the incident occurred on Oct 15, when the trader boarded an e-rickshaw at Gopalji Ka Rasta and was headed toward Sanganeri Gate. With him was a bag containing 13 packets of gemstones, mostly emeralds, of various carats.Police said the woman boarded the same e-rickshaw and travelled with the trader for a while before quietly stealing the gemstones and getting off soon after.Manak Chowk SHO Rakesh Khyalia said the distraught trader could neither recall the e-rickshaw’s registration number nor provide a clear description of anyone he suspected of the theft when he approached police later that evening.A special team comprising personnel from Manak Chowk police station and the District Special Team pored over footage from more than 200 CCTV cameras to establish the sequence of events leading to and from the crime.They eventually zeroed in on a woman who was captured on camera travelling with the trader on the same e-rickshaw. Initial suspicions were confirmed when they observed that she frequently switched vehicles and modes of transport while moving through crowded market lanes after the crime – an apparent attempt to shake off anybody following her.Once she was visually identified, police activated their informants’ network before eventually tracking her down to a hideout in the city’s Saypura slums, from where she was arrested and the stolen gemstones recovered.In all, the stolen haul included two emeralds weighing 11.5 carats, four emerald beads weighing 144.6 carats and other assorted emeralds weighing a further 942.5 carats. The combined value of the stones is estimated at more than Rs 2 crore.According to investigators, the arrested woman is part of a group of professional thieves who go about posing as shoppers in busy market areas. Their modus operandi involves identifying people likely carrying valuables, following them while often travelling with them in the same public transport, and stealing the goods at the first available opportunity.Police said the woman is being questioned and suspect she may have been involved in other thefts across the city.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Jaipur | Silver Rate in Jaipur | Bank Holidays in Jaipur | Public Holidays in Jaipur | Jaipur AQI | Weather in Jaipur | Petrol Price in Jaipur | Diesel Price in Jaipur | CNG Price in Jaipur | LPG Price in JaipurStay updated with the latest Jaipur news. articles.title: BYU QB Bear Bachmeier says Notre Dame 'disrespected' him and his family following upset win over Irish
articles.summary: Bear Bachmeier said Notre Dame disrespected him and his family during recruitment, fueling his dominant performance in BYU's 28-24 upset win.
articles.body: It's safe to say that BYU's upset win over Notre Dame on Saturday night was extra sweet for Cougars quarterback Bear Bachmeier. The signal caller was impressive during BYU’s 28-24 win over the Irish, throwing for 224 yards and a touchdown while rushing for a pair of scores in one of a handful of stunning upsets across the sport. Speaking with the media after the win, Bachmeier was asked what it was like to be a part of a field-storm-inducing victory at BYU, which is when he brought up some receipts he's kept over the years. COLLEGE FOOTBALL FACES ANOTHER CLOCK CONTROVERSY AFTER BYU UPSETS NOTRE DAME "Out of high school, Notre Dame disrespected me and my family pretty badly, and I wasn't going to lose to those guys, there was no way I was going to lose to those guys," the California native explained. Bachmeier did not go into detail about what exactly it was that the Fighting Irish allegedly did to disrespect him during his high school playing days, but it almost certainly has to be tied to his recruitment process. Notre Dame was one of over a dozen big-time programs that offered Bachmeier when he was at Murrieta Valley, and according to Adam Gorney of Rivals, he was nearing making his commitment to the Irish, but the program had Deuce Knight above him on its prospect list. Knight committed to Notre Dame in September 2023, effectively taking Bachmeier's spot, but ultimately decommitted before taking his talents to Auburn. Meanwhile, Bachmeier enrolled at Stanford, but did not stay with the Cardinal long and put his name in the transfer portal during spring practices. Bachmeier opted to transfer to BYU, along with his brother, Tiger, a wide receiver for the Cougs. articles.summary: Charanjit Singh Channi honoured with Punjab Politics Eminence Award in Dubai for his contribution to Punjab politics; Akal Takht jathedar attended.
articles.body: Chandigarh: Jalandhar MP and former Punjab chief minister Charanjit Singh Channi was honoured with the ‘Punjab Politics Eminence Award’ at an international awards ceremony in Dubai.According to the organisers, the Congress MP was recognised for his contribution to Indian politics, particularly in Punjab. Several other personalities from different fields were also honoured at the event.Akal Takht jathedar Kuldeep Singh Gargajj and Khalsa Aid founder Ravi Singh were among those present. Channi touched Gargajj’s feet to seek his blessings and spoke about his role in leading the Sikh community.Channi said the efforts of the Akal Takht jathedar and organisations such as Khalsa Aid towards social welfare were a source of inspiration. articles.title: Kerala water authority plans Rs 45cr tertiary sewage recycling project in Thiruvananthapuram
articles.summary: Kerala Water Authority plans Rs 45cr, 15 MLD tertiary sewage recycling plant at Muttathara, Thiruvananthapuram, with 10km pipelines; tendering underway.
articles.body: Thiruvananthapuram: Kerala Water Authority (KWA) is planning a Rs 45 crore sewage recycling project at Muttathara to ease the pressure on the city’s freshwater supply, with the airport, railways, Titanium, Veli Industrial Estate and Technopark identified as prospective consumers of recycled water.The project involves setting up a 15 million-litre-a-day (MLD) tertiary treatment plant to further treat partially treated sewage effluent from the existing 107 MLD sewage treatment plant at Muttathara. The proposed facility will use advanced treatment technology to improve the quality of the effluent, making it suitable for non-drinking purposes, subject to prescribed quality standards.The existing plant currently produces around 60 MLD of partially treated sewage effluent that can undergo further treatment. However, the proposed facility, with a design capacity of 15 MLD, will process only a portion of this output and will not treat the entire volume generated by the existing plant.KWA has held discussions with the prospective consumers, who have agreed to purchase the recycled water provided the authority ensures supply through pipelines, a KWA engineer said. The tariff to be charged for the treated water, however, is yet to be finalised.The project initially envisaged transporting recycled water to the establishments through tankers. During the final rounds of discussions, the prospective consumers sought pipeline connections, prompting KWA to include a network spanning around 10km in the project, the engineer said.“Economic activities and the establishment of industries, services sectors and shopping centres have increased the demand for water. During peak summer, with the available supply, we often struggle to meet the demand. We hope this project will help us keep pace with the rising demand,” the KWA engineer said.The proposed arrangement could help major establishments meet part of their water requirements using recycled sewage instead of depending entirely on conventional freshwater supplies. This could also leave more freshwater available for households and other consumers, particularly during summer, when demand rises and the authority faces pressure to maintain uninterrupted supply.The initiative is expected to promote wastewater reuse by turning partially treated sewage into a resource for commercial and industrial activities. The airport, Railways, Titanium, Veli Industrial Estate and Technopark are among the establishments identified as potential buyers, though the actual volume supplied to each will depend on the final arrangements and the availability of treated water.The administrative sanction for the project has been completed, and the tendering process is under way. The construction start date will be fixed after the tender is finalised. The project schedule stipulates 12 months for construction.“The finalisation of supply agreements and tariffs with the prospective consumers is yet to be finalised,” a KWA engineer said.Stay updated with the latest Thiruvananthapuram news.
